target.title: fix(diagnostic): avoid model-call stream hot-path object copies
target.body:
Related: #91588
Related: #97211

## What Problem This Solves

Diagnostic model-call accounting still uses object rest/spread on two hot paths:

- `responseStreamChunkByteLengthUnchecked()` copies every non-delta stream chunk that carries an accumulated `partial` snapshot.
- `baseModelCallEvent()` builds optional fields through conditional spread objects.

Issue #91588 contains field evidence around V8 `Runtime_CopyDataPropertiesWithExcludedPropertiesOnStack` / dictionary-key collection that points at the stream-chunk copy site. This PR removes those copies while preserving diagnostic byte-accounting and event-field behavior.

Scope boundary: this is a narrow diagnostic hot-path mitigation. It does not close #91588, prove a multi-day RSS plateau, change memory-pressure thresholds, fix Gateway startup readiness, or address session/plugin/native-memory retention.

## Current Issue Context

All current comments in #91588 and #97211 were reviewed before this refresh.

- #91588 now contains several distinct observations: the original multi-day RSS/OOM report, dictionary-mode/object-copy CPU evidence, plugin-owned accumulation findings, plugin-disabled core-memory reports, baseline/threshold concerns, startup-readiness reports, and native/off-heap RSS observations. Those reports do not establish one universal root cause.
- This PR only addresses the directly implicated diagnostic copy/spread surface and deliberately makes no broader causality claim.
- #97211 is closed without merge. It targeted the same two hot paths. This PR remains a separate, non-closing contribution with its own current-head semantic coverage and proof; no reason for #97211's closure is inferred here.

## Why This Change Was Made

The implementation avoids reading or copying accumulated `partial` snapshots during diagnostic byte accounting. Common scalar-only chunks are counted directly without allocating a snapshot object or per-property result wrappers. Shapes requiring full `JSON.stringify` semantics use a proxy that lazily hides `partial`; non-extensible or non-configurable shapes use a descriptor-preserving snapshot fallback.

The event-base change assigns optional fields directly into one object instead of creating conditional spread objects.

## User Impact

Long-lived Gateway workloads should avoid one source of diagnostic stream copy churn and repeated `partial` snapshot reads. The change is diagnostic-internal and does not intentionally alter provider transport, model output, persisted session data, or public configuration.

## Breaking Changes

None expected.

## Implementation

- Replace `{ partial, ...snapshotlessChunk }` with direct byte counting for own enumerable scalar data fields other than `partial`.
- Use module-level sentinel values instead of allocating a tagged wrapper for each scalar property on the common path.
- Preserve `JSON.stringify` omission behavior for unsupported object-property values.
- Preserve value-level `toJSON(key)` behavior, including monkey-patched BigInt `toJSON`.
- Preserve callable chunk-level `toJSON` behavior while hiding `partial` lazily.
- Preserve descriptors and own enumerable `__proto__` data keys in the snapshot fallback without mutating `Object.prototype`.
- Build `baseModelCallEvent()` once and assign optional fields conditionally.
- Add focused coverage for getter safety, JSON semantics, `toJSON`, non-configurable/non-extensible shapes, and `__proto__` data keys.

## Latest-Main Compatibility

Current PR head: `efde77185d32b8a0cb46ebda8fc57a1562be7f21`
Rebase baseline: `2a7132a43f536a88746c7c3905860df13faa1548`

The branch was recreated on the then-current official `openclaw/openclaw:main`. Recent main changes in the same module were reviewed and preserved:

- #103073 adds provider-request timeline events.
- #103476 propagates the managed model-call `requestId`.
- #105937 adjusts adjacent test fixture imports during plugin-loader cleanup.

The rebased diff still changes only:

- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.model-diagnostic-events.ts`
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.model-diagnostic-events.test.ts`

Runtime callers reviewed: normal embedded attempts in `attempt.ts` and compaction calls in `compact.ts`. Adjacent contracts reviewed: diagnostic event inputs, plugin model-call hooks, trace/request context propagation, run-progress activity, and the focused model-call diagnostic tests.

## Validation

### Exact-head runtime proof

- [GitHub Actions proof run](https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29252481937) — passed.
- Artifact: `pr99154-model-diagnostic-runtime-proof-29252481937-1` (`summary.md`, `baseline.json`, `head.json`).
- Environment: GitHub Actions `ubuntu-24.04`, Node `v24.18.0`, `workflow_dispatch`.
- Proof binding: baseline `2a7132a43f536a88746c7c3905860df13faa1548`; PR head `efde77185d32b8a0cb46ebda8fc57a1562be7f21`.

Edge behavior:

- Baseline partial-getter edge failed as expected: expected `34` bytes, no byte metric emitted.
- PR head partial-getter edge passed: expected/actual `34 / 34`.
- Own non-enumerable chunk `toJSON` passed: `54 / 54`.
- Inherited/prototype chunk `toJSON` passed: `35 / 35`.
- Non-configurable `partial` snapshot fallback passed: `54 / 54`.
- Own enumerable `__proto__` data-key edge passed: `73 / 73`.
- Value-level `toJSON(key)` passed: `68 / 68`, observed key `value`.
- BigInt `toJSON(key)` passed: `52 / 52`, observed key `value`.

Synthetic model-call stream:

- 50,000 representative non-delta chunks were drained through `wrapStreamFnWithDiagnosticModelCallEvents()`.
- Baseline and PR head both reported `responseStreamBytes=2911669`.
- Duration: baseline `186.21 ms`; PR head `187.02 ms` (`0.4%` higher). This is short-run signal only, not a speedup claim.
- RSS delta: baseline `33,255,424` bytes; PR head `9,773,056` bytes. This is short-run signal only, not multi-day RSS proof.

Large accumulated-partial workload:

- 10,000 chunks with large `partial` snapshots.
- Baseline `partialReads=10000`; PR head `partialReads=0`.
- Expected/actual PR-head byte count: `527780 / 527780`.
- Duration: baseline `42.76 ms`; PR head `37.49 ms`.

### Repository checks

All visible workflows for the current head completed successfully, including:

- [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29252476048)
- [CodeQL](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29252475951)
- [CodeQL Critical Quality](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29252475932)
- [OpenGrep — PR Diff](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29252476168)
- [Workflow Sanity](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29252475981)
- [Real behavior proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29252473098)
- [Dependency Guard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29252473051)
- [Security Sensitive Guard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29252473180)

Current-head check-run read-back: `68` success, `35` skipped, `1` neutral, `0` failed, `0` pending (`104` total).

### Local pre-checks

- `git diff --check`
- `oxfmt --check` on both changed files
- `oxlint` on both changed files: `0` warnings, `0` errors

No local build or broad test suite was used as delivery evidence; repository tests and type/build checks run in GitHub Actions.

## Evidence Source Map

- Field/native-stack evidence and evolving root-cause discussion: #91588.
- Overlapping closed candidate and its review history: #97211.
- Exact-head runtime/benchmark proof: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29252481937.
- Focused regression coverage: `attempt.model-diagnostic-events.test.ts`.
- Repository CI/checks: current PR head `efde77185d32b8a0cb46ebda8fc57a1562be7f21`.

## Data Model / Migration Compatibility

No persisted schema, session serialization, vector/embedding metadata, migration, store, or upgrade path changes. The implementation constructs transient diagnostic events and byte counts in memory; the test changes exercise that transient behavior only.

## Risk

- Unusual provider chunk shapes can exercise the proxy or descriptor-preserving fallback. Focused tests and exact-head proof cover getter failures, callable `toJSON`, value-level `toJSON(key)`, BigInt behavior, non-configurable `partial`, and own enumerable `__proto__` data keys.
- The scalar fast path avoids snapshot and tagged-wrapper allocation, but nested/accessor/custom-serialization shapes still require a proxy or snapshot fallback to preserve semantics.
- Short synthetic timings and RSS deltas are noisy. This PR should be evaluated on eliminated snapshot reads/copies and byte-equivalence, not as a broad performance or leak-resolution claim.
- #91588 includes memory contributors outside this module; those remain open and separately owned.

## Rollback

Revert this PR. No data or config migration is required.

## Docs Updated

No user documentation changes are required. The patch changes internal diagnostic accounting and focused tests only.

## Review Context Addressed

- Current-head proof is bound to the exact rebased PR SHA.
- The body no longer attributes all #91588 memory observations to this hot path.
- Persistent-data compatibility is stated explicitly.
- Callable chunk-level `toJSON`, lazy getter ordering, value-level `toJSON(key)`, BigInt `toJSON(key)`, non-configurable `partial`, and own enumerable `__proto__` semantics have regression coverage.
- Latest-main provider timeline and managed request-correlation changes remain present after rebase.
- The common scalar path no longer allocates one tagged result object per property.

## Not Tested / Limitations

- No multi-day Gateway RSS/heap/native-memory soak.
- No production workload claim.
- No claim that this fixes all memory growth, tool degradation, threshold warnings, startup readiness, session retention, plugin retention, or native/off-heap RSS behavior in #91588.
- Short-run benchmark and RSS values are reported for transparency and are not treated as stable performance guarantees.
